# Metadata exploration
![](images/explore.png){style="border-radius: 15px; width: 200px; background-color: white" fig-align="center"}

The choice of metadata is always important.
This is especially so when you are using mixed models like with [MaAsLin3](/maaslin3/maaslin3.qmd).

It is good to test and see if any metadata variables are collinear/aligned.
Generally we want to avoid using multiple variables that are collinear in statistical formulas.

As an extreme example you would not want to use date of birth and age.
A less clear example would be if you had read depth and agar concentration.
In this case you are likely to have more organisms growing on higher agar concentrations and therefore more reads.
In the end it is up to you to decide which variables to include or not.

In this part we'll carry out some quick metadata correlation analysis.
We'll do this for the [Rhizosphere soil metadata](/maaslin3/dataset.html#rhizosphere-soil).
However, we'll include even more metadata variables that were present in the original dataset.

For this we'll use functions from the R package [`variancePartition`](https://github.com/GabrielHoffman/variancePartition) which was developed for gene expression analysis.

## Conda environment
<center>
![](../images/mamba_logo.png){style="border-radius: 15px; width: 200px; background-color: white"}
</center>

For this section you'll need a new conda environment and `jupyter-notebook` session.

Before continuing save then close and halt all your open jupyter notebooks.
Then close your current jupyter-notebook server.
To carry this out:

1. Click on the terminal running the server
2. Press "ctrl + c"
3. Press y then enter to confirm closing the server

To run the new jupyter notebook:

1. Open a new terminal (right click on background and choose "Terminal")
2. Run the following command to activate the `metadata_explore` environment: `. usemetaexplore`
3. Move directory into "adv_R_comm": `cd ~/adv_R_comm`
4. Create a new directory for the analysis: `mkdir meta_exploration` 
5. Open jupyter-notebook: `jupyter-notebook`
6. With the jupyter notebook file explorer move into your "meta_exploration" directory

The next page is carrying out some metadata correlation.
